mainTopic: An idol that broke by itself: the מחלוקת of רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש, and the rule that a ספק cannot override a ודאי
overview: The גמרא first asks why the משנה forbids a hand-shape or foot-shape, when broken pieces of idols are permitted. שמואל answers that the משנה means shapes standing on their own base, so they were made that way and are not broken pieces. Next comes a מחלוקת about an idol that broke by itself. רבי יוחנן forbids it because nobody did ביטול. ריש לקיש permits it because the owner surely gave up on an idol that could not even save itself. רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from the story of דגון and from the משנה about found statue fragments, and ריש לקיש answers both. The גמרא then defends רבי יוחנן. An idol was certainly worshipped, and a ספק of ביטול cannot override that ודאי. It tests this rule against the case of a חבר who died and left produce, and answers in two ways. Finally it begins another challenge to the rule from a story told by רבי יהודה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Aren't these just broken pieces?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the משנה forbids a hand-shape or foot-shape, since broken pieces of an idol are permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: But these are just broken pieces!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's rule that a hand-shape or foot-shape is forbidden. Such a shape looks like a piece broken off an idol, and broken pieces are permitted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה permits found fragments of statues, and according to שמואל broken pieces of idols are permitted too. Yet the משנה forbids hand and foot shapes. A hand or foot found alone looks like it broke off a whole statue, so it should fall under the permitted category of broken pieces.

keyTerms.meaning: Broken pieces or fragments
But isn't it so that…? This word opens a challenge.
They are

phrases.english: But aren't they fragments!
phrases.notes: "They" means the hand-shapes and foot-shapes the משנה just said are forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the משנה's ruling on hand and foot shapes.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that a hand-shape or foot-shape is forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A lone hand or foot looks like a broken-off piece, and broken pieces are permitted. So why forbid it?

steps.title: They stand on their own base
steps.stepSummary: שמואל explains that the משנה is talking about hand or foot shapes standing on their own base.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמואל explained: the case is where they stand on their bases.
steps.whatsHappening: שמואל answers the question. The משנה is talking about a hand or foot that stands on its own base.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If a hand or foot has its own base, it was made that way from the start. It is a complete object of worship, not a piece that broke off. That is why it stays forbidden while real broken pieces are permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained it, meaning he showed how to read the משנה
Their base or pedestal
Standing

steps.whatToRemember: A hand or foot that stands on its own base is a whole idol in itself. It is not a broken piece, so it stays forbidden.

phrases.english: Shmuel interpreted it:
Where they stand on their pedestals.

steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrows the case of the משנה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The hand or foot is a broken-off piece, so it should be permitted.
steps.terutzMaskana: It stands on its own base, so it was made that way and is a complete object of worship.

steps.title: An idol that broke by itself
steps.stepSummary: A new מחלוקת: רבי יוחנן forbids an idol that broke on its own, and ריש לקיש permits it.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was stated: if an idol broke by itself, רבי יוחנן says it is forbidden and רבי שמעון בן לקיש says it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: an idol that broke on its own, with no person breaking it. Two אמוראים argue about whether it is still forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually only a נכרי's act of cancelling (ביטול) makes an idol permitted. The question is whether breaking by itself works the same way. רבי יוחנן says it is still forbidden, and ריש לקיש says it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: An idol or object of idol worship
That broke by itself
Forbidden / permitted (for benefit)

phrases.english: It was stated: an idol that broke by itself,
Rabbi Yoḥanan says: it is prohibited,
phrases.notes: This means it is forbidden to get any benefit from it.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מוּתֶּרֶת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: it is permitted.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic connected to the idea of broken idols.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: an idol that broke by itself stays forbidden. ריש לקיש: it is permitted.

steps.title: The reasons on each side
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן says no one cancelled the idol. ריש לקיש says the owner surely gave up on it, since it could not even save itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן forbids it because it was never cancelled. ריש לקיש permits it because the owner surely cancelled it, thinking: it could not save itself, so how can it save me?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the reasoning behind each side of the מחלוקת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both agree that an idol needs ביטול, cancelling by its worshipper, to become permitted. They argue about whether we can assume it happened. רבי יוחנן says no one actually cancelled it. ריש לקיש says we can safely assume the owner gave up on an idol that could not even protect itself.

keyTerms.meaning: It was cancelled. This means its status as an idol was removed.
Presumably, we can assume
He surely cancelled it
Saved / can save

steps.confusionAlert: ריש לקיש is not saying that breaking cancels an idol automatically. He says the owner surely cancelled it in his mind once he saw it break.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the main question is about ביטול: does it need to be clearly done, or can we assume the owner gave up on the idol?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan says: it is prohibited,
since it was not revoked.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ אָמַר: מוּתֶּרֶת,
phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish says: it is permitted,
presumably he revoked it,
saying to himself:
It could not save itself,
can it save that man?
phrases.notes: "That man" is the worshipper's way of saying "me."

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אָמַר: אֲסוּרָה, דְּהָא לָא בָּטְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning behind the two rulings in step 3.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן: no ביטול happened, so it stays forbidden. ריש לקיש: we assume the owner cancelled it, so it is permitted.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges from the story of דגון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן points out that after דגון broke, its priests still honored it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: "The head of דגון and both palms of his hands were cut off." And it is written: "Therefore the priests of דגון do not step on the threshold of דגון."
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש with a פסוק. After the idol דגון broke, its worshippers still honored it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש assumed that a worshipper gives up on an idol once it breaks. But the פסוקים show the priests of דגון kept honoring it after it broke, even refusing to step on its threshold. So worshippers do not necessarily give up on a broken idol.

keyTerms.meaning: דגון, the idol of the פלשתים
Threshold. This is the place the priests would not step on (see the פסוק).
And it is written

phrases.aramaic: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan raised an objection to Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish:
"And the head of Dagon and both the palms of his hands
were cut off, etc.",
and it is written: "Therefore they do not tread,
phrases.notes: שמואל א 5:5. The rest of the פסוק says they will not step on דגון's threshold.

phrases.english: the priests of Dagon, etc."!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks ריש לקיש's reasoning from step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's assumption that a worshipper gives up on an idol that broke by itself.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: דגון broke by itself, yet its priests kept honoring it. So breaking does not prove the worshippers gave up on it.

steps.title: The פלשתים moved their worship to the threshold
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the דגון story proves nothing. The people did not respect the broken idol; they started worshipping the threshold instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Is that a proof? There they left דגון and worshipped the threshold, because they said: 'The spirit of דגון has left it and come to sit on the threshold.'
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers רבי יוחנן's proof from step 5. He says the priests were not honoring the broken idol at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן thought the priests avoided the threshold out of respect for the broken דגון. ריש לקיש says they avoided it because the threshold itself became their new god. So the broken idol may still have been given up on, which fits ריש לקיש's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there a proof from there? A way of rejecting a proof.
Threshold, the doorstep where דגון fell.
Its guardian spirit, the power they believed lived in the idol.
Left it, abandoned it.

phrases.english: He said to him: Is there a proof from there?
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is the speaker, answering רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: There, it is because they left the Dagon
and worshipped the threshold,
for they said this:
Its spirit has left Dagon,
phrases.notes: Literally 'its prince', the power they thought was inside the idol.

phrases.english: and came and settled itself on the threshold.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from דגון brought in step 5.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof from the דגון story only.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The priests' behavior shows worship of the threshold, not respect for the broken idol.

steps.title: Challenge from the משנה about found statue fragments
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן quotes the משנה that statue fragments are permitted. He reads it to mean that fragments of a real idol are forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: He challenged him: One who finds fragments of statues, these are permitted. This implies that fragments of an idol are forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן brings a new attack on ריש לקיש, this time from a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה permits fragments of ordinary statues. רבי יוחנן reads the opposite case into it: fragments of something known to be an idol stay forbidden. That matches his view that a broken idol is still forbidden, against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: Broken pieces of statues.
This implies. It introduces a reading of what a text implies.

phrases.english: He challenged him: One who finds fragments of statues,
phrases.notes: רבי יוחנן is quoting the משנה.

phrases.english: these are permitted.
This implies that fragments of an idol are forbidden!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the דגון proof fails, רבי יוחנן tries a new proof from a משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's ruling that an idol that broke on its own is permitted.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה stresses 'statues'. That suggests fragments of a real idol would be forbidden, even though they are broken.

steps.title: Reading the משנה as following רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש says the משנה is contrasting fragments with whole statues, not with idol fragments. It follows רבי מאיר, who forbids whole statues.
steps.simpleTranslation: Don't say it implies that idol fragments are forbidden. Rather say it implies that the statues themselves, when whole, are forbidden. This unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers by changing what the משנה is being contrasted with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה's point is: pieces are permitted, but whole statues are forbidden. That is רבי מאיר's view from the earlier משנה, where he forbids all statues. So the משנה says nothing about fragments of a real idol, and ריש לקיש's view stands.

keyTerms.meaning: Don't say... rather say. A formula for rereading a text.
An unnamed משנה, with no author given.
The statues themselves, when whole.

phrases.aramaic: לָא תֵּימָא שִׁבְרֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: Do not say that fragments of an idol are forbidden;

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא אֵימָא: הָא צְלָמִים עַצְמָן אֲסוּרִין,
phrases.english: rather say: this implies that the statues themselves are forbidden,
and the unnamed משנה follows רבי מאיר.
phrases.notes: In the earlier משנה, רבי מאיר forbids all statues, since they may be worshipped once a year.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא תֵּימָא שִׁבְרֵי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֲסוּרִין, אֶלָּא אֵימָא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rereads what the משנה implies and names its author as רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The משנה contrasts statue fragments with idol fragments, so idol fragments are forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: The משנה contrasts fragments with whole statues, following רבי מאיר, and says nothing against ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Learning the רבנן's view from רבי מאיר
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יוחנן answers this: רבי מאיר forbids statues but allows their fragments, so the רבנן should forbid an idol but allow its fragments.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי יוחנן, how does he answer this? From רבי מאיר we can learn about the רבנן. Doesn't רבי מאיר say statues are forbidden but statue fragments are permitted? Then according to the רבנן too, an idol is forbidden and its fragments are permitted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to רבי יוחנן and asks how he deals with this reasoning. The next step gives his answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי מאיר, a statue is like an idol, yet its pieces are allowed. The רבנן should apply the same pattern to a real idol: the whole idol is forbidden but its broken pieces are allowed. That supports ריש לקיש and puts pressure on רבי יוחנן.

keyTerms.meaning: We can learn for them, carry over a rule to them.
The Sages who argue with רבי מאיר.
Its broken pieces.

steps.confusionAlert: This is not ריש לקיש speaking. The גמרא itself is asking how רבי יוחנן would answer this reasoning.

phrases.english: And רבי יוחנן,
phrases.notes: The question left unsaid is: how does he answer the following?

phrases.english: from רבי מאיר we can learn for the Rabbis:
Didn't רבי מאיר say:
statues are forbidden, fragments of statues are permitted?

phrases.aramaic: לְרַבָּנַן עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה נָמֵי הִיא אֲסוּרָה
phrases.english: So for the Rabbis too, the idol itself is forbidden
and its fragments are permitted!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מִדְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר נִשְׁמַע לְהוּ לְרַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on step 8's claim that the משנה follows רבי מאיר and turns it against רבי יוחנן.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's ruling that a broken idol stays forbidden.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If רבי מאיר allows the pieces of something he forbids when whole, the רבנן should likewise allow the pieces of a forbidden idol.

steps.title: Statues are doubtful, but an idol was certainly worshipped
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן's side answers that the רבי מאיר comparison fails. Statues may never have been worshipped, and even if they were, they may have been nullified. An idol was certainly worshipped, so only its nullification is in doubt, and a ספק cannot override a ודאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: How can you compare them? With statues, maybe they were worshipped and maybe not. Even if they were, maybe they were nullified. An idol was certainly worshipped, so who says it was nullified? That is a doubt against a certainty, and a doubt cannot remove a certainty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן against the question from step 9. It shows why fragments of a real idol are stricter than fragments of statues.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With statues there are two layers of doubt: maybe they were never worshipped, and maybe they were nullified. With a real idol, the worship is certain and only the ביטול (nullification) is doubtful. So the idol's forbidden status is a ודאי that a mere ספק of ביטול cannot cancel.

keyTerms.meaning: How can you compare? This rejects a comparison.
They nullified them, so they removed their idol status.
A doubt
A certainty
A doubt cannot take something out of its certain status.

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the general principle אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי, which the rest of this section tests.

phrases.english: How can these be compared?
There, say that they worshipped them,
phrases.notes: "There" means the statues that רבי מאיר forbids.

phrases.english: or say that they did not worship them;
and even if you say they worshipped them,
say that they nullified them.
An idol was certainly worshipped,
so who is to say that they nullified it?
It is a doubt against a certainty,
and a doubt does not remove a certainty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9's question on רבי יוחנן by pointing out a difference between statues and idols.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between cases: statues involve a double doubt (worship and ביטול), while an idol involves a doubt (ביטול) against a certainty (worship)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since רבי מאיר permits fragments of the statues he forbids, the רבנן should permit fragments of a real idol.
steps.terutzMaskana: Statue fragments involve two doubts, while an idol's worship is certain, and a ספק cannot override a ודאי.

steps.title: Challenge from a חבר's produce: a doubt does override a certainty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא questions the rule that a ספק cannot override a ודאי. A ברייתא says that produce left by a חבר who died is presumed tithed. Yet that produce was certainly טבל at first, and whether he tithed it is only a doubt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Does a doubt really not override a certainty? A ברייתא teaches: if a חבר died and left a storehouse full of produce, even produce from that same day is presumed tithed. Here the produce was certainly untithed, and it is only a doubt whether he tithed it, yet the doubt overrides the certainty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the rule just used in step 10. It quotes a ברייתא where a doubt seems to win over a certainty.
steps.deeperAnalysis: All produce starts out as טבל, which is a certainty. Whether the חבר separated מעשר before he died is only a doubt. Since the ברייתא still treats the produce as tithed, it seems a ספק can override a ודאי after all.

keyTerms.meaning: A person trusted to be careful about tithes and purity
A storehouse or granary
Only from that day, meaning freshly brought in
Presumed to be properly tithed
Untithed produce (טבל)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's point is that the produce is presumed tithed even though it came in that very day, when it might seem he had no time to tithe it.

phrases.english: And does a doubt not remove a certainty?
But isn't it taught in a ברייתא:
A חבר who died
and left a storehouse full of produce,
even if the produce is from that same day,
it is presumed to be properly tithed.
But here, it was certainly untithed,
maybe he tithed it,
maybe he did not tithe it,
and the doubt comes and removes the certainty!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין סָפֵק מוֹצִיא מִידֵי וַדַּאי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the principle used in step 10's answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: The principle אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In the ברייתא, certain טבל is treated as tithed based only on a doubt, so a doubt does override a certainty.

steps.title: A חבר certainly tithes, so it is certainty against certainty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the חבר case is not a doubt against a certainty. We are certain the חבר tithed, based on רבי חנינא חוזאה's חזקה that a חבר never lets untithed produce leave his hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: There it is a certainty against a certainty, because he certainly tithed it. This follows רבי חנינא חוזאה, who said: we presume that a חבר does not let anything untithed leave his hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from the ברייתא. The rule from step 10 stays in place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חזקה about a חבר is strong enough to count as a ודאי that he tithed. So the ברייתא is a certainty overriding a certainty, not a doubt overriding one. The idol case is still a true doubt against a certainty.

keyTerms.meaning: A certainty against a certainty
A firm presumption
From under his hand, meaning out of his control or possession

steps.whatToRemember: A ספק cannot override a ודאי. A strong חזקה, like a חבר's care with מעשר, counts as a ודאי. So fragments of a real idol stay forbidden according to רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: There, it is a certainty against a certainty,
because he certainly tithed it,
in line with רבי חנינא חוזאה,
as רבי חנינא חוזאה said:
There is a presumption about a חבר
that he does not let out something untithed
from under his hand.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 by redefining the חבר case as certainty against certainty.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: the חזקה gives a certainty
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The חבר's tithing is only a doubt, so a doubt overrides the certain טבל status.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי חנינא חוזאה's חזקה makes the tithing a certainty, so the principle אין ספק מוציא מידי ודאי holds.

steps.title: Second answer: maybe the produce was never untithed at all
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: the חבר's produce may never have been טבל, because he may have used רבי אושעיא's trick of bringing grain in with its chaff. So the case is ספק against ספק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or you can say: maybe the produce was never טבל to begin with, so it is a doubt against a doubt. It is possible the חבר did what רבי אושעיא allows. A person may use a trick with his grain and bring it in while it is still in its chaff, so that his animal can eat from it and it is free from מעשר.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second, different answer to the question from the חבר who died. It says that maybe there was never a certainty there at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question assumed the produce was surely טבל at first, and only the tithing was in doubt. This answer removes that certainty. Maybe the חבר brought the grain in still in its chaff, so it never had to be tithed. Now both sides are doubts, so the rule that a ספק cannot beat a ודאי was never tested here.

keyTerms.meaning: "And if you want, say". This introduces a second, alternative answer.
Produce that must be tithed and has not been tithed yet. It is forbidden to eat.
A doubt against a doubt. Neither side is certain.
Uses a legal trick, a permitted way to avoid an obligation.
Chaff, the husk around the grain kernel.
Tithes, the portions of produce that must be separated.

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not say the חבר certainly used the trick. It only says he might have. That doubt is enough to turn the case into ספק against ספק.

phrases.english: And if you wish, say:
from the start the produce was not untithed (טבל),
so it is a doubt against a doubt.
phrases.notes: Doubt one: was it ever טבל? Doubt two: if it was, did he tithe it?

phrases.english: It is possible that he acted like Rabbi Oshaya,
who said: A person may use a trick with his grain
and bring it in while it is still in its chaff,
phrases.notes: Grain still in its chaff is not finished yet, so the duty to tithe has not started.

phrases.english: so that his animal may eat from it
and it is exempt from tithes.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא: מֵעִיקָּרָא לָא טְבִילִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second answer to the challenge in step 11, alongside the חזקה answer of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case: it removes the assumed certainty, so the case becomes ספק against ספק.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The produce was surely טבל, so presuming it tithed would mean a ספק overriding a ודאי.
steps.terutzMaskana: The produce may never have been טבל, because of רבי אושעיא's trick. So there is no ודאי in this case, and the rule is not challenged.

steps.title: New challenge: a ברייתא where a doubt seems to override a certainty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks again whether a ספק really cannot override a ודאי, and starts quoting a ברייתא from רבי יהודה about an incident with a maidservant.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is it really true that a doubt does not override a certainty? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה said, there was an incident with the maidservant...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new attack on the rule that a ספק cannot override a ודאי. This line only sets up the challenge; the story of the ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After answering the challenge from the חבר, the גמרא brings another source against the same rule. It introduces a story told by רבי יהודה about a maidservant. The full challenge will only become clear once the story is told.

keyTerms.meaning: A doubt cannot take something out of its certain status.
An incident, a real-life case that is brought as proof.
A maidservant.

phrases.english: And is it so that a doubt does not override a certainty?
But it was taught in a ברייתא: Rabbi Yehuda said:
There was an incident with the maidservant
phrases.notes: The story continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין סָפֵק מוֹצִיא מִידֵי וַדַּאי? וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After steps 12 and 13 answered the חבר challenge, this step brings a new source against the same rule from step 10.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule from step 10 that a ספק cannot override a ודאי.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא from רבי יהודה describes an incident that seems to let a doubt override a certainty. The details come on the next amud.
